reconstructed by hand), then tearing the probe worktree down. The new
`--scratch-timeout-s` will be >=2x the slowest single step.

likely speed every git op here, but it is disruptive to ~15 concurrent

## New bound: 900s, and the arithmetic behind it

Measured max single step 118.2s at load ~45. Observed load on this box has
ranged 41-78 during this round, so ~2x slower at the peak gives ~240s;
applying the project's p90-style x2 dispersion default gives ~480s. 900s is

about.

Generosity is free here: the flag bounds only a WEDGE. A healthy checkout
returns in ~2 min regardless of the bound, so a larger number cannot slow a
working run — it only widens the window before a genuinely stuck git command
is killed. That asymmetry is the same one that made the 23400s gate fence
the right call.
